title: GitHub - JasonXuDeveloper/Nino: The fastest binary serializer for C#. Source-generated, zero-allocation: services, RPC, messaging, caching, storage, Unity and Godot.
excerpt: The fastest binary serializer for C#. Source-generated, zero-allocation: services, RPC, messaging, caching, storage, Unity and Godot. - JasonXuDeveloper/Nino
content_html:
Why Nino

  • Fastest. Up to 7.2× faster serialization than MemoryPack, and up to 9.5× faster deserialization into existing objects. Benchmarks
  • Safe on untrusted input. Crafted bytes cannot crash the process, read past the input, allocate out of proportion or name a type to create; every invalid input throws one NinoDataException. Untrusted data
  • Zero allocation. Serialize into an IBufferWriter<byte>, deserialize into existing or pooled objects: nothing allocated per call, thread-safe, with no locks on the hot path. Zero allocation
  • Everything at compile time. No reflection, no IL emit, no registration, no init call: works on IL2CPP, Native AOT and HybridCLR hot updates, and compiles up to 221× faster than v3. Platforms
  • The same bytes everywhere. Identical bytes on every runtime and CPU, and from Go, Rust and TypeScript through the code nino-gen writes for your types. Other languages
  • Rich types that evolve. Polymorphism without tags, keyed and version-tolerant types, reference tracking, every BCL collection. Supported types
  • Mistakes caught as you type. 33 analyzer diagnostics, many with a one-click fix. Analyzers

Install

dotnet add package Nino --prerelease    # .NET and Godot: the runtime and the generator
openupm add com.jasonxudeveloper.nino   # Unity 2022.3+

Nino v4 is a prerelease, so --prerelease is required: without it NuGet installs 3.9.x, which cannot read or write v4 data. Optional packages: Nino.Immutable (System.Collections.Immutable), Nino.AspNetCore (MVC formatters, Minimal API bodies and results), Nino.Codegen (your types as TypeScript, Go or Rust after each build; Nino.Codegen.Tool is the same as the nino-gen command). Installation for .NET, Unity and Godot.

Quick start

using Nino.Core;

[NinoType]
public sealed class Order
{
    public long Id;
    public string Customer;
    public List<OrderLine> Lines;
}

byte[] bytes = NinoSerializer.Serialize(order);
Order copy = NinoDeserializer.Deserialize<Order>(bytes);
NinoDeserializer.Deserialize(bytes, ref copy); // fills the same instance in place

Polymorphism needs no tags: a value declared as its base is read back as its runtime type.

[NinoType] public abstract class Message { public int Seq; }
[NinoType] public sealed class Chat : Message { public string Text; }

byte[] bytes = NinoSerializer.Serialize<Message>(new Chat { Text = "hi" });
Message msg = NinoDeserializer.Deserialize<Message>(bytes); // a Chat again

Next: your first types, evolving data, reference tracking, pooling and the advanced guides.

AI coding assistants

Nino ships a skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and other agents:

npx skills add JasonXuDeveloper/Nino

The nino-serialization skill teaches your assistant to declare [NinoType]s, pick the format for data that outlives a release, use the fast and zero-allocation forms, and fix every NINO diagnostic. The docs are written for models too: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, and every page as Markdown (add .md to its URL).

Benchmarks

BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.8, .NET 10.0.14, server GC, Intel Xeon 6973P-C 3.54 GHz; Nino v4 and MemoryPack 1.21.4 in one run, Nino 3.3.13 from NuGet directly before it on the same machine. Payloads are about the same size (SimpleClass: 1,069 bytes in v4, 1,152 in v3, 1,148 in MemoryPack). Every case and the method: docs/v4-benchmarks.md; the notes of each release carry that release's numbers.

Every case, Arm64, MessagePack and protobuf-net: .NET benchmarks; Unity with Burst; Go, Rust and TypeScript. Arrays of tuples and structs and string conversion use AVX-512, AVX2, SSSE3, Arm64 and WebAssembly SIMD (Burst kernels in Unity), with portable code writing the same bytes elsewhere: SIMD.

Built for
⚙️ Services & IPC No per-call allocations, safe concurrent use; ASP.NET Core bodies as application/x-nino.
🌐 RPC & networking Straight into a PipeWriter, pooled messages, and a crafted message throws instead of taking the server down.
📨 Message queues · 🗄️ Caching · 💾 Storage Polymorphic events, small payloads, and formats that let fields be added, reordered and removed across releases.
🧩 Web, Node, Go & Rust Types and codecs generated after each build, so browsers and services read and write the same bytes as .NET.
🎮 Unity 2022.3+, Mono and IL2CPP, HybridCLR without an init call, Burst SIMD kernels, AnimationCurve and Gradient built in.
👾 Godot 4 (.NET) A regular NuGet package; Vector3, Transform3D and other math structs are copied as raw memory.

Compared with MemoryPack

MemoryPack's README now calls it "a high-performance serialization format for trusted data only" (MemoryPack README); Nino is built for data from network peers and user files (details).

Nino v4 MemoryPack 1.21.4
Untrusted input built for it: bounded allocation and stack, one exception type trusted data only, per its README
Serialize classes and polymorphic types 3.5–7.2× faster
Deserialize classes and polymorphic types 1.7–2.1× faster
Raw struct arrays at least on par without padding (a block copy in both); padding zeroed padding copied as is, in the platform's layout
Deserialize into existing objects 0 B, up to 9.5× faster (in place) overwrite mode: clears collections and allocates their elements again
Polymorphism automatic type ids, any base class or interface, generic bases included [MemoryPackUnion] tags you maintain, not on generic types
Keyed members, reference tracking, object pools ✅ version tolerance and circular references, no pools
Unity ✅ 2022.3+, one OpenUPM package, netstandard2.0 and 2.1 ✅ 2022.3.12f1+, NuGetForUnity plus a git package, netstandard2.1

While benchmarking we found three types MemoryPack 1.21.4 does not round-trip (BigInteger, BitArray on .NET 10, tuples between runtimes); Nino writes them by value. The full comparison covers them, what MemoryPack has that Nino does not, and how to switch. Also compared: MessagePack and protobuf-net.

v4 vs v3

v4 is a rewrite of the runtime and the generator. Its binary format is not compatible with v3.

v4 vs v3 (3.3.13)
Serialize 2.11× faster (class), 2.49× faster (class array), 1.37× faster (struct), on par (struct array)
Deserialize 1.55× faster (class), 1.55× faster (class array), on par (struct), on par (struct array), while adding reference tracking, reuse deserialization and payload validation
Compiling the generated code 51× faster at 330 types (42.9 s → 0.84 s), 221× faster at 1,100 types (462 s → 2.1 s)
Running the generator 3.1× faster; after an edit, only that type is re-generated (8.3× faster)
Generated code 14× smaller source, 5× smaller IL

Everything new: what's new in v4, the changelog and the migration guide; internals are in docs/v4-design.md.

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. CONTRIBUTING.md covers building, the test matrix and releasing.

基准测试

BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.8, .NET 10.0.14, server GC, Intel Xeon 6973P-C 3.54 GHz; Nino v4 and MemoryPack 1.21.4 in one run, Nino 3.3.13 from NuGet directly before it on the same machine. Payloads are about the same size (SimpleClass: 1,069 bytes in v4, 1,152 in v3, 1,148 in MemoryPack). Every case and the method: docs/v4-benchmarks.md; the notes of each release carry that release's numbers.

Every case, Arm64, MessagePack and protobuf-net: .NET benchmarks; Unity with Burst; Go, Rust and TypeScript. Arrays of tuples and structs and string conversion use AVX-512, AVX2, SSSE3, Arm64 and WebAssembly SIMD (Burst kernels in Unity), with portable code writing the same bytes elsewhere: SIMD.

专为
⚙️ Services & IPC No per-call allocations, safe concurrent use; ASP.NET Core bodies as application/x-nino.
🌐 RPC & networking Straight into a PipeWriter, pooled messages, and a crafted message throws instead of taking the server down.
📨 Message queues · 🗄️ Caching · 💾 Storage Polymorphic events, small payloads, and formats that let fields be added, reordered and removed across releases.
🧩 Web, Node, Go & Rust Types and codecs generated after each build, so browsers and services read and write the same bytes as .NET.
🎮 Unity 2022.3+, Mono and IL2CPP, HybridCLR without an init call, Burst SIMD kernels, AnimationCurve and Gradient built in.
👾 Godot 4 (.NET) A regular NuGet package; Vector3, Transform3D and other math structs are copied as raw memory.

Compared with MemoryPack

MemoryPack's README now calls it "a high-performance serialization format for trusted data only" (MemoryPack README); Nino is built for data from network peers and user files (details).

Nino v4 MemoryPack 1.21.4
Untrusted input built for it: bounded allocation and stack, one exception type trusted data only, per its README
Serialize classes and polymorphic types 3.5–7.2× faster
Deserialize classes and polymorphic types 1.7–2.1× faster
Raw struct arrays at least on par without padding (a block copy in both); padding zeroed padding copied as is, in the platform's layout
Deserialize into existing objects 0 B, up to 9.5× faster (in place) overwrite mode: clears collections and allocates their elements again
Polymorphism automatic type ids, any base class or interface, generic bases included [MemoryPackUnion] tags you maintain, not on generic types
Keyed members, reference tracking, object pools ✅ version tolerance and circular references, no pools
Unity ✅ 2022.3+, one OpenUPM package, netstandard2.0 and 2.1 ✅ 2022.3.12f1+, NuGetForUnity plus a git package, netstandard2.1

While benchmarking we found three types MemoryPack 1.21.4 does not round-trip (BigInteger, BitArray on .NET 10, tuples between runtimes); Nino writes them by value. The full comparison covers them, what MemoryPack has that Nino does not, and how to switch. Also compared: MessagePack and protobuf-net.

v4 vs v3

v4 is a rewrite of the runtime and the generator. Its binary format is not compatible with v3.

v4 vs v3 (3.3.13)
Serialize 2.11× faster (class), 2.49× faster (class array), 1.37× faster (struct), on par (struct array)
Deserialize 1.55× faster (class), 1.55× faster (class array), on par (struct), on par (struct array), while adding reference tracking, reuse deserialization and payload validation
Compiling the generated code 51× faster at 330 types (42.9 s → 0.84 s), 221× faster at 1,100 types (462 s → 2.1 s)
Running the generator 3.1× faster; after an edit, only that type is re-generated (8.3× faster)
Generated code 14× smaller source, 5× smaller IL

Everything new: what's new in v4, the changelog and the migration guide; internals are in docs/v4-design.md.
